policy: Preserve named game identities when catalog retrieval returns only lexical or identifier-shape neighbors. Generic physical role families do not automatically establish equivalence to a named character. Compact droid identifiers require full normalized-code agreement, and incidental English words such as Hood or Codebreaker must not dominate person-level matching.

systemic_findings: Compact droid identifiers need full normalized-code agreement; shared digits and letters are weak evidence.
A generic physical role family must not be promoted to an exact named-character counterpart without direct identity evidence.
Surnames that are also clothing terms, such as Hood, need person-level parsing before apparel matching.
Master Codebreaker and DJ are distinct characters even though both share a codebreaking role.
Named astromechs must remain identity-distinct despite shared R-series body families.
